answers.question: What's the Technical to Onsite conversion for Engineering roles?
answers.answer:
Engineering has three roles: Senior Backend Engineer, Firmware Engineer, and Data Platform Engineer.

Combined, **5 of 10 candidates (50%) who reached Technical went on to Onsite.**

| Role | Reached Technical | Reached Onsite | Conversion |
|---|---|---|---|
| Senior Backend Engineer | 4 | 1 | 25% |
| Firmware Engineer | 4 | 3 | 75% |
| Data Platform Engineer | 2 | 1 | 50% |
| **Engineering total** | **10** | **5** | **50%** |

- For comparison, the company-wide Technical to Onsite rate is 45.8% (11 of 24).
- The sample is small, so the per-role rates swing a lot. One candidate changes a role's rate by 25 to 50 points.
- I calculated the Engineering total from the raw counts. The tool only reports per-job rates and an all-jobs total.

answers.question: Where in the funnel do we lose the most candidates?
answers.answer:
**The biggest loss is at the first step, Applied → Recruiter Screen.** Only 43 of 120 applicants (35.8%) get a screen, so 77 candidates drop out there. That is about 64% of all applicants and more than every later stage combined.

| Stage | Reached | Conversion from previous stage | Lost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Applied | 120 | n/a | n/a |
| Recruiter Screen | 43 | 35.8% | 77 |
| Technical | 24 | 55.8% | 19 |
| Onsite | 11 | 45.8% | 13 |
| Offer | 4 | 36.4% | 7 |
| Hired | 3 | 75% | 1 |

- **Offer stage:** The 36.4% conversion looks as bad as the screen, but it is 4 of 11 candidates, so it is a very small sample. Onsite → Offer is the weakest rate after the first step.
- **Applied → Screen by job:** The drop is consistent across jobs, between 22% and 48%. The worst is Partnerships Manager at 22.2% (2 of 9). Data Platform Engineer (28.6%) and Senior Backend Engineer (30%) are also low.
- **Candidates still in Applied:** 10 are still sitting in Applied, so the real loss may be slightly smaller than the table shows. Some of them may not have been reviewed yet.

The data shows where candidates drop out, not why. I can't tell whether the cause is weak applicant quality or slow screening. I can run the stuck-candidates report to check whether the Applied stage is backed up.

answers.question: What share of applicants end up hired, and how many offers were accepted?
answers.answer:
**About 2.5% of applicants end up hired: 3 of 120. Three of the 4 offers (75%) were accepted.**

- **Offers:** 4 applications reached the Offer stage. They were Senior Backend Engineer, Firmware Engineer, HR Business Partner and Equipment Maintenance Lead.
- **Accepted:** 3 of those reached Hired, one each for Senior Backend Engineer, Firmware Engineer and HR Business Partner.
- **Not accepted:** The Equipment Maintenance Lead offer didn't convert. No one is still sitting at the Offer stage, so it was probably declined or withdrawn. The data doesn't say which.

The tool has no explicit "offer accepted" field, so I counted reaching Hired as acceptance. The 2.5% also counts everyone still in the pipeline, so it will probably rise as the open roles fill.

answers.question: How does the Account Executive pipeline look?
answers.answer:
**Account Executive (Job 8, Business Development, open)**

| Stage | Reached | Currently in stage | Conversion from previous stage |
|---|---|---|---|
| Applied | 21 | 2 | n/a |
| Recruiter Screen | 10 | 1 | 47.6% |
| Technical | 6 | 1 | 60.0% |
| Onsite | 2 | 0 | 33.3% |
| Offer | 0 | 0 | 0% |
| Hired | 0 | 0 | n/a |

**Takeaways**
- **Active candidates:** Only 4 are still in play. Two are in Applied, one is in Recruiter Screen and one is in Technical. Nobody is in Onsite or Offer.
- **No offers yet:** Two candidates reached Onsite, and neither moved to Offer. The other 2 of those 4 were presumably rejected or withdrew.
- **Conversion compared with other jobs:** The Applied to Recruiter Screen rate of 47.6% is above the all-jobs average of 35.8%. The Technical to Onsite rate of 33.3% is below the all-jobs average of 45.8%, but the sample is small.
- **Stuck candidates:** Two of the four active candidates have waited over a week.
  - **Oakley** has been in Recruiter Screen for 22.2 days. This is the longest wait of any Account Executive candidate, and the longest across all jobs.
  - **Zephyr** has been in Applied for 11.7 days.

**Suggested next steps:** Schedule or close out Oakley's screen, and triage Zephyr's application. The pipeline is thin, so you may also want to source more candidates. Only one person is in the Technical stage, and nobody is at Onsite.

I can also pull time-to-fill for Business Development if that would help.
